name: MI Ambivalence Conversation
purpose: Run the Motivational Interviewing layer of conversation — spirit, four processes (engaging, focusing, evoking, planning), OARS micro-skills, DARN-CAT change-talk detection with commitment-slope tracking, and runtime fidelity gates (reflection-to-question ratio toward ~0.84, complex reflections >= 50%, per Aimi/MISC-2 evidence) — with a hard gate that MI techniques without spirit are not MI.
representative_examples: User says 'I know I should exercise more, but I never have energy' — evoke desire/reasons before any planning; tag sustain talk, explore it, never fight it.
When reflection-to-question ratio drops below ~0.84 across a window, downgrade questions to complex reflections and log the fidelity miss.
When commitment slope is falling, defer planning and return to evoking (Amrhein 2003: slope is prognostic).
failure_hints: If the user starts defending the status quo, the agent has argued against resistance.
If the user's change talk is all repetition of agent-supplied reasons, evocation has become prescription (disingenuous change talk).
If the user agrees to plans they later abandon within 24h, planning may have run ahead of readiness (Eiroa-Solans 2025 decay).
source_influences: Motivational Interviewing: Miller & Rose 2009 relational pathway (VERIFIED, empathy r=.82)
Aimi/MISC-2: Shenoi 2026 ratio 0.84, complex reflections 66.7% (VERIFIED, Recent_Evidence_Digest Area 1)
Miller & Mount 2001 self-report vs coded proficiency (VERIFIED)
triggers: motivational barrier identified by diagnosis skills
readiness assessment required before planning or practice
user stuck between reasons for and against
completion_conditions: spirit gate passed before each technique
four processes advanced in order without skipping evoking
DARN-CAT tags written for change and sustain talk
readiness verdict recorded; planning gated on it

governance.rule: No AtomicOp executes on high-meaning tasks (identity, values, commitments, interpretive closure) without a Human_Empowerment_Boundary check first
